locator: §2.2, 'On that basis he claimed that there could be no moral knowledge or error (Carnap 1937; 23–24 & 29).'
interpretation: Carnap, an early non-cognitivist (a prescriptivist: 'Killing is evil' means 'Do not kill'), drew from his semantics the consequence that there is no moral error. Read as: no one is in error about a moral matter. Carnap's 'could be no' is modal; only the non-modal claim is formalized. This is the conclusion EMOTIVISM-EXCLUDES-MORAL-ERROR derives from O'Connor's emotivism. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
